gaps.gap: SessionRow's attention-level map omits `waiting-perm` (permission required). A session in waiting_on_permission falls through `ATTN[status] ?? 0` to level 0 (idle, no rail) — but the attention ladder ranks permission as level 4. The most consequence-bearing 'needs-a-human' state would render with idle visual weight, breaking attention-first ordering.
gaps.kit_evidence: components/objects/SessionRow.jsx ATTN map line 12 (no 'waiting-perm' key) + level = ATTN[status] ?? 0 (line 32)
gaps.doc_ref: readme.md §3 Attention Ladder ('4 failed/blocked/conflict & permission'); ARCHITECTURE.md §5.1 Session state waiting_on_permission; PRD §5.2 attention-first ordering
gaps.recommendation: Change the kit: add 'waiting-perm' (and a generic fallback for any unmapped waiting_on_* state) to SessionRow's ATTN map at level 4, mirroring AttentionMarker's intent.
gaps.for_tasks_gen: The attention-level derivation (used by SessionRow, sidebar rows, queue items, graph nodes) MUST map EVERY one of the 17 canonical Session states to a ladder level, with no silent fall-through to idle. waiting_on_permission = level 4; waiting_on_human_input = level 5; waiting_on_external_service must have an explicit non-idle level. Add a test that every Session enum value resolves to its specified ladder level.
